name: pdfjs-dist
source: the npm registry tarball pdfjs-dist-6.5.438.tgz, unpacked; every file below is byte-identical to the file of the same path under the tarball's package/ directory

files.why: the library (display layer): loaded by the review page with import() when a document is viewed as a PDF
the library worker (parsing, text content): started by pdf.min.mjs as a same-origin module worker
the ZapfDingbats standard font, likewise (check marks of form fields drawn on the page)
the Symbol standard font, which the library fetches when a document uses it without embedding it (system fonts stand in for the other standard fonts)
licence of the two standard fonts (BSD-3-Clause)
licence of the library wrapper of that decoder (Apache-2.0)
licence of the library wrapper of that decoder (BSD-2-Clause)
JBIG2 image decoder in plain JavaScript, loaded by the worker for the same reason
JPEG 2000 image decoder in plain JavaScript, loaded by the worker because the viewer runs with useWasm false (no WebAssembly, so no wasm-unsafe-eval in the policy)

not_included: build/pdf.mjs, build/pdf.worker.mjs and their source maps: the minified builds are the same code
build/pdf.sandbox*.mjs and wasm/quickjs-eval.*: document scripting is never run
build/pdf.renderer*.mjs: pages are drawn on the main thread (disableWorkerRendering)
wasm/*.wasm and iccs/: no WebAssembly is used (useWasm false), so colour profiles fall back to the device colour spaces
cmaps/: predefined CJK character maps, which documents in English do not need

standard_fonts/ other than Symbol and ZapfDingbats: with useSystemFonts the library never fetches the other Type 1 fonts, and the four Liberation Sans files (GPL-2.0 with a font exception) are only its last url() source after the local() system fonts it names for the Helvetica family, so a computer with none of those draws such text in its generic sans-serif
web/ (the full viewer and its stylesheet), image_decoders/, legacy/ and types/
